doc.title: Ashley Keating and Allan Whitworth Interview, 1963-03-22

title: Australian band styles and Ken Colyer's 1962 convention visit
summary: Keating contrasts the older Australian West Coast style with newer Lewis-style bands, and explains how the convention committee chose Colyer after approaching several Americans.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: What are the other Australian bands like in general?

At the current time, there seems to be a, a fair, uh, swing towards the, uh, pianoless rhythm section and the, uh, Lewis-style clarinet. Uh, of course, there's still plenty of the older Australian-style jazz band, which is based on the, the Lou Watters West Coast style. I think if there is an Australian jazz style, that is it, uh, as exemplified by Graham Bell, Frank Johnson, and other bands, which I can't think of at the moment. Southern Jazz Band. The Southern Jazz Band, that's right, Dave Dalwitz's band. Uh, that type of, uh, style is, actually, I'd say, the Australian style. Uh, but, of late, in all the capital cities on the East Coast, that's Melbourne, Sydney, and Brisbane, there has been at least one or two Lewis-style bands functioning with a pianoless rhythm section, as I said, and the Lewis-style clarinet and strong vibrato from the trumpeter. Uh, they seem to meet, or to me, anyway, there seems to be a little, uh, either jealousy or disapproval on the part of the older jazz enthusiast, that's to say, the man of about, uh, 40, 45. Uh, he regards the other style as being, uh, the heritage of the young musician, and, uh, to suddenly come up with, with this style that is different. Uh, they seem to, uh, view it with a certain disdain. Uh, I think that was made pretty clear with the relatively cool reception Collier got from this vintage of jazz fan when he came to our convention in 1962.
How did Ken Collier get that? Whose idea was that?

Uh, the committee, uh, that was elected at the 1961 convention was instructed, uh, by the outgoing committee to, uh, make a search, uh, worldwide, uh, and to bring, uh, as a featured guest, a jazz man of note from some foreign country, preferably America, but, uh, England, or, as long as he was, uh, a jazz man with an international reputation. Uh, I believe several, uh, American jazz men were approached. Kid Orie was, uh, not feeling well. Turk Murphy was too busy. Uh, Louis Armstrong, of course, had other work. Uh, Lizzie Miles was asked also, but couldn't make it. George Lewis, uh, didn't feel he could make the trip. Uh, and, until finally it was narrowed down to white musicians, uh, such as Jimmy McPartland and Max Kaminsky, uh, both of who, uh, did reply, uh, both of whom, I suppose I should say, did reply, but, uh, made demands that the committee couldn't really meet. Uh, at a later date, McPartland came up with more suitable terms, but, uh, Collier had already been approached, uh, and had, uh, accepted to come. I believe the fee was a thousand pounds. That was to cover his first-class return airfare, uh, plus first-class accommodation, uh, and, uh, his entertainment for the five days he was there, or, it turned out to be longer. He was there about eight days, I think. Uh, I don't think there will be another guest artist, uh, asked, really. Uh, the committee that has just gone out, uh, instructed the incoming committee that, uh, if possible, it was to be avoided. Uh, apparently, public opinion was, or opinion amongst the jazz fan, that it was, uh, too expensive, and sooner or later, uh, the committee was going to run out of money at this rate. Seems a bit of a shame, really. I think they could have got a, perhaps a Negroid jazz man this time.
